conclusion:
MEMO: /Users/agedvagabond/Developer/exchange-hours-research/cme-globex/trade-types/U8-cross-zone-design.md
1. U-8's premise is false. A StaticHoursProfile carries one tz, but a KEY is not limited to one profile: six shipped modules (ICE Endex, ICE Abu Dhabi, Eurex fixed income, Eurex benchmark-index, B3, BMV) already express two-zone grids as an offset-selected profile pair via schedules::timeline::reference_delta_seconds.
2. RECOMMEND Option G - keep tz America/Chicago, ship two static profiles per shape, select with reference_delta_seconds. Zero public API change, zero serde change, no existing key moves, no migration; EurexFixedIncome is the key-side precedent.
3. It is law-clean. The seasonal switch asserts NO date, so LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES is satisfied; revisions! carries only sourced launch days (SER-5788 2011-06-13, SER-5794 2011-07-11, SER-9380 2024-06-17, Globex 20171016 2017-10-23, Globex 20190211 2019-02-25). LAW-DETERMINISM and LAW-PANIC hold: reference_delta_seconds is pure and resolves through the total mk_local_open.
4. Twelve affected SHAPES, not eight (fifteen moving rule endpoints, since 6EB's interruption and each crypto stop have two ends that move together): the five TAM shapes, DVT/E3T, FTC, Nikkei and TOPIX BTIC, crypto BTIC London and APAC, plus 6EB (an INTERIOR London-anchored gap, missing from U-8's list).
5. NOT affected: TMAC, TACO, equity/sector/AIR BTIC, credit BTIC, crypto BTIC New York, commodity-index BTIC - America/New_York shares Chicago's DST calendar, so a constant -1h offset is exactly representable. Do not spend the mechanism there.
6. Drift quantified: London-anchored shapes have 2 states (241 vs 20 weekdays of 2026); no-DST Asian anchors have 2 large states (170 vs 91). US/UK misalignment is 21 or 28 CALENDAR days a year = 15 or 20 affected weekdays (14 or 21 in spring, always exactly 7 in autumn), stable 2010-2030.
7. Cost of a single grid: 20 hours/year of FALSE-CLOSED executable window (London, aligned grid) or false-open on 241 weekdays (misaligned grid); for Asia, an hour wrong on 35-65% of weekdays. AGENTS.md ranks executable-window gaps highest.
8. Two structural facts make it exact: no session ever spans an offset change (US transitions 02:00 local Sunday, UK 01:00 UTC = Sat 20:00 CDT, both while shut), and the swap never flips wrap/no-wrap, so trade dates are stable. Nearest miss is the Tokyo-anchored Nikkei/TOPIX BTIC close at 00:30 CT, with CLC at 01:00 second - assert wrap agreement, loudest on the Tokyo pair.
9. New first-hand evidence: GCD id=8407 closed@10:02 (2026-10-26 wk), 09:02 (2026-12-07 wk), 10:02 (2027-03-15 wk) with open@17:00 unchanged throughout; FTC id=7956 closed@03:00 Oct / 02:00 Dec. The SPRING window is measured for the first time. CME's Energy TAM FAQ publishes both Central values itself for CLS/BZS and CLC.
10. Follow-ups to open as issues (LAW-FOLLOW-UPS-ARE-ISSUES): session_profile's doc claims a clock-less current table equals the timeline at any instant - already false for EurexFixedIncome half the year; the same for hours_for_market_hours_key's 'one grid at every instant'; 6EB's addition to U-8; the un-re-verified copper marker DST carve-out; the near-midnight wrap caveat. Test set: ten assertions in section 4, pinning aligned summer, aligned winter, autumn and spring misalignment, all four transition weekends date-aware (misalignment entry and exit in both spring and autumn, on the shipped endex_calendar_scans_reselect_both_mismatch_entries_and_exits template), the no-span invariant, profile-pair equality except close_ssm, trade-date stability, serde, and a mutation check.
11. This is the SECOND pass over gate U8-cross-zone-design; the memo at the path above was revised in place rather than rewritten. Re-hashed all stored artifacts (pass), re-read the CME service bytes first-hand rather than quoting the draft, re-derived the tz arithmetic with a second independently written script, and re-read every cited in-repo line at HEAD fdc5408. Four non-load-bearing corrections landed (calendar-day count, nearest-midnight boundary, call-site count, FAQ publication date) and section 4 T5 was widened from two transition weekends to four. The recommendation - Option G - is unchanged and now rests on two independent derivations of the same numbers.

NOTHING here is a dated cutover: the seasonal swap must never enter a revisions! table or HISTORICAL_CUTOVERS.
dead_ends: Rejected representations, with why, so nobody re-opens them. (A) Per-rule tz on SessionRule - changes the crate's atom, its public wire format and every one of the 94+31 profile tables to serve nine keys; breaks wraps_to_next_day() (next local day in WHICH zone) and normal_week_rule_intervals' nominal-86400s axis; rewrites every line of the golden file, destroying the reviewability the golden file exists for. (B) Profile-level close_tz on StaticHoursProfile/MarketHours - MarketHours::new takes 7 positional args so an 8th is breaking; MarketHours.tz silently changes meaning from 'the venue's zone' to 'the open's zone', altering trade_date and is_closed_all_day_on for external callers; resolve_rule_bounds must pick a civil close day in a foreign zone, which is genuinely ambiguous near Chicago midnight (Nikkei/TOPIX BTIC at 00:30 CT, CLC at 01:00) and fails silently as a 24-hour session rather than an error. (C) Split each shape into two profiles joined by a rule - a profile has one tz, so two profiles means two keys and then NO key answers 'is CLL tradeable at 11:00 CT'; splitting the session instead leaves the foreign anchor untouched and needs joins_adjacent_same_kind, documented as an identity capability and not a shape heuristic. (D) Express the whole grid in the close's zone and accept a drifting Chicago open - the exact mirror image, same magnitude, worse target (the error moves to the START of the executable window), and it drags DayPolicy and trade dates into London dates for a US-holiday venue; note the symmetry, since a one-tz profile means whichever zone you pick the other endpoint still needs two values, so (D) is the recommended design with the roles swapped, minus the benefit. (E) Model the close as a separate 'marker close' event - inverts LAW-SESSION-NOT-EXPIRY: CME says 'trading halts at the marker time, daily', which IS session language, so this would make the crate answer 'open' for an hour when CLL cannot trade. (F) Defer with the shapes UNMAPPED - honest and law-clean, and still correct for any shape whose hours are not sourced in session language, but unnecessary for representability. Retrieval dead ends this session: the trading-hours service rejects requests without pageSize (HTTP 400) and rate-limits aggressively per IP (429 after ~2 rapid calls); the COMEX metals-marker page could not be re-fetched live today and its copper London/New-York DST carve-out remains second-hand from the shape-queue JSON; no product id was located for CLL/CLS/CLC, so those three were not measured first-hand.
